Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior

Enum Class OngoingBehavior

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<OngoingBehavior>
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.OngoingBehavior
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<OngoingBehavior>, Constable
public enum OngoingBehavior extends Enum<OngoingBehavior>
The named eye behaviors that last as long as the mob stays in some state, as opposed to the one-shot EyeBehavior expressions. Each client derives a state from what vanilla already syncs, so nothing about one crosses the mod's own network except its server switch, sent with the eye definitions in BehaviorSettings. A state never blocks an expression: the client folds it in on top of whatever plays.

Each entry owns its id, its server switch, and the vanilla state that drives it (level(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity)); how the eyes show it lives with the eye simulation in GooglyTracker. The one state with a server-reported half is ANGER: anger vanilla keeps on the server reaches clients through EyeAngerPacket, and the tracker folds it into this level.

This type must stay free of client-only imports: the server class-loads it to build the synced settings.

    A skeleton drawing a ranged weapon, or a player drawing a bow, closes the eye away from the arm holding it.
